description: §42.3.5 / §42.3.6 absence-safe render, ABSENT path. The plain-optional cell is `not`. `${@user?.name}` (optional-chain, §42.3.6) short-circuits to `not` and renders NOTHING (no-value-no-output, §6), so #opt reads only "Name:". `if=@user` is falsy so the guarded subtree DOES NOT EXIST IN THE DOM (§17.1) — #guard and its #inner both have count 0, and the guarded `${@user.name}` interp never runs. Both forms compile clean (no E-TYPE-046). Twin of optional-member-access-render — the empty/fallback render.
rationale: §42.3.6: `recv?.field` short-circuits to `not` when the receiver is `not`; §6 no-value-no-output renders nothing. §42.4: `not` is falsy, so `if=@user` leaves the guarded subtree unmounted — §17.1: "When `expr` evaluates to false, the element is NOT rendered. It does not exist in the DOM." §17.2 draws the contrast: `show=` hides, `if=` removes. Absence renders as nothing, never the string "undefined" (§42.8).
